transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood Solutions); Dr. Priya Shah (CTO), Mark Liu (Head of Infra), Elena Gomez (Security), Tom Reyes (ML)

Summary (auto): High-level discovery for Private deployment. Customer wants a VPC-hosted Redwood control plane or private control plane with private endpoints, strict EU data residency for some workloads, and integration with their KMS. Focus on peering, PrivateLink endpoints, transit gateway, and SSO.

Transcript:
00:00 Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Ava from Redwood, AE on the Veridian account. Today we'll do a quick discovery on Private/VPC options, and Liam will dig into the network/security stuff. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Dr. Priya Shah: Good, thanks. Quick note — we have a few constraints: PHI handling in EU for a subset of our patients and we need on prem-like controls, SSO through our IdP, and encryption keys must be customer managed.
00:27 Liam O'Connor: Got it. Thanks Priya. Do you have a preference between Dedicated reserved capacity versus a private deployment inside your VPC? We typically see two patterns: Redwood Dedicated (isolated GPUs we manage) or Redwood Private (control plane in our VPC / customer's VPC).
00:45 Mark Liu: We're leaning toward Private — we want the control plane to sit in our AWS account with private endpoints, no public internet egress for token exchange. Also need to know about per-region availability — we run most prod workloads in eu-west-1 and a secondary region in eu-central-1.
01:05 Liam O'Connor: Okay. For Private we support a few models: VPC peering, Transit Gateway attachment, and AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). Each has trade-offs. Peering is simple but scales poorly across many accounts; Transit Gateway is great for many VPCs and central routing; PrivateLink gives you interface endpoints per service — less routing complexity but you manage endpoints.
01:28 Elena Gomez: Important: we need audit logs, access logs, and to bring our KMS for model encryption. Can you integrate with an external HSM or KMS?
01:38 Sofia Chen: Yes — we have KMS integrations for Redwood Private. We can support customer-managed KMS keys, and we can surface audit logs to your CloudWatch/S3 or a syslog collector. We'll share our security pack with the SOC2 report.
01:50 Tom Reyes: A couple of infra questions — do you require NAT/GW for egress, and how do you handle model updates / kernel downloads? We prefer to avoid any public egress from our prod VPCs.
02:05 Liam O'Connor: For Private, there are two common approaches: 1) Pull model artifacts via a NAT or egress path you control (we can pull from an S3 bucket on your account, or you can mirror models into your private repo), or 2) use VPC endpoints to S3/STS so no public internet is needed. If you want zero egress, we can arrange for an in-account S3 bucket with a cross-account role.
02:28 Mark Liu: We use Transit Gateway for inter-VPC connectivity. Would Redwood attach to our TGW or do you require peering?
02:36 Liam O'Connor: We can attach to your Transit Gateway. Typical setup: we create service endpoints in a management VPC in your account, attach to TGW, or use interface VPC endpoints. We'll provide Terraform/CF templates. I'll share specifics after this call.
02:51 Dr. Priya Shah: Data residency — we need EU-only for certain patient data. Can we restrict model serving for those requests to eu-west-1?
03:00 Ava Martinez: Absolutely. We can pin model variants and routes by region. Our routing policy supports region-specific enforcement and fallbacks to a secondary region only if you opt in. We'll document the routing controls.
03:15 Elena Gomez: About identity — SSO and RBAC. We use Okta with SCIM. Do you support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning?
03:24 Sofia Chen: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. For Private we can integrate with your IdP and enforce RBAC roles that mirror your org hierarchy.
03:35 Mark Liu: Network specifics: what CIDR ranges do you need, and do you require dedicated ENIs?
03:41 Liam O'Connor: We ask for a /22 or /21 range per deployment depending on autoscale needs — the template will have recommended sizes. We often use ENIs for interface endpoints. If using PrivateLink, ENIs are created in subnets you designate. We'll need route table access for the subnets.
03:57 Tom Reyes: Latency — for inference workloads with sensitive PHI, we want sub-50ms p99. Can we get that with Private in eu-west-1?
04:07 Liam O'Connor: Sub-50ms p99 depends on model size and GPU placement, but Private inside your region should generally reduce network latency vs hosted across the internet. We'll work with you on model selection and instance sizing. For strict latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated Reserved capacity in-region. But Private in-region with good instance types should be fine for many use cases.
04:30 Dr. Priya Shah: What about fallbacks? If capacity in eu-west-1 is saturated, do we fail open to Hosted in another region?
04:39 Ava Martinez: You control fallback policy. We can set strict no-fallback for sensitive workloads, or allow failover to a compatible model in a mirrored region. We'll capture that in the SLA/rollout config.
04:52 Elena Gomez: Encryption — KMS key access patterns, do you hold any key material?
05:00 Sofia Chen: No, for customer-managed KMS we do not hold key material. We request IAM roles to decrypt as-needed. HSM integrations are supported for Private if you require FIPS/HSM attestations. We'll include details in the security pack.
05:17 Mark Liu: What's required from networking folks?
05:20 Liam O'Connor: We'll need: VPC ID, CIDR ranges, subnets for control plane endpoints, route tables, whether TGW is used, any firewall/NSG rules, and the account ID you want us to deploy into. Also proxy/NAT details if egress is restricted.
05:36 Mark Liu: Understood. We'll send current VPC layout.
05:39 Dr. Priya Shah: Compliance — we need audit trails for model inputs/outputs for a subset of requests (retention 7 years). Is that feasible?
05:51 Sofia Chen: We can store logs to a customer-controlled S3 and set retention lifecycles. For PHI we recommend encryption at rest with your KMS and restricted IAM. We also have data retention policies that can be configured per-route.
06:05 Tom Reyes: A bit about model ops — how are model updates handled? We need control windows and can opt out of auto-updates in prod.
06:15 Liam O'Connor: You can pin model versions; we support canary rollouts and A/B testing managed through the Console. For Private, we can coordinate optional auto-update windows or manual rollout.
06:28 Mark Liu: Anything on egress IPs? Our security team requires a whitelist of destination IPs for outbound connections.
06:35 Liam O'Connor: For Private deployments in your account, egress is under your control; for some control plane communications we may need to reach Redwood endpoints for telemetry unless you opt into an air-gapped control plane. We'll provide a small range of IPs if needed and also have a private control plane option with no public egress.
06:54 Elena Gomez: Can we get sample IaC?
06:57 Liam O'Connor: Yes — I'll attach Terraform and CloudFormation snippets.
07:00 Ava Martinez: Quick recap of next steps — we'll send the security pack and SOC2, Liam will prepare VPC peering/PrivateLink + TGW templates, and we'll set up a network deep-dive for next week.
07:12 Dr. Priya Shah: Great. One more — pricing expectations for Private vs Dedicated?
07:18 Ava Martinez: I'll send a pricing sheet. Private has a platform fee plus infra; Dedicated is more commit-based. We'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
07:28 Mark Liu: Cool. Thanks.
07:32 Ava Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
07:36 (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present — e.g., 'Transit Gateway' heard as 'transit gatewayy' in a few places.
